newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore property stocks weaken on poor sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Singapore property stocks weaken on poor sentiment.

text.p: Singapore property index plunged 1.9 percent, or 13.55 points, to 689.22 in afternoon trade on Tuesday on poor sentiment surrounding the sector as well as the general market, dealers and analysts said.
At 0720 GMT, the index was trading at 689.58, down 10.86 points or 1.55 percent.
Property heavyweights like City Developments Ltd and Singapore Land fell Singapore $0.20 and S$0.30 respectively to S$13.70 and S$6.70.
"The market is down on talks that recent launches, even at good property sites like Balmoral Road, had not been well-received," said a dealer.
Balmoral Road is in one of Singapore's prime residential districts.
Dealers said while some reports said recent launches along Balmoral Road were above S$2,000 per square foot (psf), many were in fact sold around S$1,700.
"Fundamentals in the property market are not good," ING Barings analyst Lim Chung Chun told Reuters.
"I think the situation will get worse. We are seeing an over-supply building up, especially for private residential," Lim said. Things could worsen in another 12 months, he added.
